newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgarian-American bank has 5.5 mln lev net profit.
newsitem.headline: Bulgarian-American bank has 5.5 mln lev net profit.

text.p: The Bulgarian-American Credit Bank (BACB) posted 5.5 million levs net profit for 1996 after paying taxes of 3.7 million levs, figures from the bank's income statement showed on Tuesday.
Year-end figures published in the State Gazette showed the bank's income was 14.7 million levs and its expenses, including taxes totalled 9.2 million levs.
BACB assets totalled 999.6 million levs of which short-term investments amounted to 994.9 million levs at the the end-1996, balance sheet figures showed.
The bank's own capital totalled 989.7 million levs.
On July 11, 1996 the Bulgarian National Bank (BNB) granted a limited licence to the BACB, allowing it to extend credits up to the limit of its own funds.
The bank was not permitted to attract funds from individuals and companies.
The BACB was licensed with a share capital of 450 million levs, of which over 90 percent were owned by the Bulgarian-American Investment Fund.
Last month the BACB said it planned to raise capital to 10 billion levs to comply with an anticipated rise of BNB minimum capital requirements for local banks. @
The BNB minimum capital requirement for domestic and international operations is now set at 2.2 billion levs and for a domestic licence at 1.4 billion levs. -- Sofia Newsroom, (++359-2) 911 88
